title: Are you addicted to your phone
titleChinese: 你是不是玩手机上瘾了？
paragraphs: How often do you check your phone? According to a study led by Nottingham Trent University in Britain, the average person looks at their device 85 times a day, browsing the internet or using apps. Updating their status on social media platforms also made people reach for their electronic companion frequently.

Even the study's participants thought that was a lot: this figure is twice as often as they thought they did. Our phones might be shaping our behaviour more than we realise, and changing the way we interact with people right next to us.
Do you actually look at your surroundings more than at your phone? Is it rude to check your phone when someone is talking to you?

Sherry Turkle interviewed hundreds of college students about this. She's a clinical psychologist and a professor of social studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. They talked about something they called 'the rule of three'.

The rule has to do with being considerate to others in spite of the allure of the little flat box. Turkle explains: "If you go to dinner with friends, you don't want to look down at your phone until you see that three people are looking up in the conversation. So there's a new etiquette where you don't look down unless three people are looking up in order to keep a little conversation alive."

Actually, if you are clever enough you might use your phone as a tool to connect with people next to you. How about showing them pictures stored in its memory? Sharing a bit of your life with them can bring you closer together. And you can also invite everyone to take a selfie with you.

But the best thing to deal with mobile phone addiction is to go cold turkey and leave the machine behind occasionally or just switch it off and keep it firmly in your pocket for a while. Who knows... 'life' might be what happens when you are too busy staring at a small screen.

vocabulary.entry: browse the internet [phr.] /braʊz ði ˈɪntənet/ 浏览互联网 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He spends hours browsing the internet every day.
vocabulary.translation: 他每天花几个小时浏览互联网。

vocabulary.entry: reach for [phr.] /riːtʃ fɔː/ 伸手去拿 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: She reached for her phone as soon as it rang.
vocabulary.translation: 电话一响，她就伸手去拿手机。

vocabulary.example: All participants in the study signed a consent form.
vocabulary.translation: 所有研究参与者都签署了同意书。

vocabulary.example: Childhood experiences shape our adult personalities.
vocabulary.translation: 童年经历塑造了我们成年后的性格。

vocabulary.entry: interact with [phr.] /ˌɪntərˈækt wɪð/ 与……互动 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Teachers should interact with students in a positive way.
vocabulary.translation: 教师应以积极的方式与学生互动。

vocabulary.entry: clinical psychologist [n.] /ˈklɪnɪkəl saɪˈkɒlədʒɪst/ 临床心理学家 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The clinical psychologist diagnosed the patient with anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 临床心理学家诊断该患者患有焦虑症。

vocabulary.entry: the rule of three [n.] /ðə ruːl əv θriː/ 三规则 (固定搭配；专有名词)
vocabulary.example: According to the rule of three, you should wait until three people are looking up.
vocabulary.translation: 根据三规则，你应该等到有三个人抬头。

vocabulary.example: It was very considerate of you to offer help.
vocabulary.translation: 你主动提出帮助，真是体贴。

vocabulary.entry: allure [n.] /əˈljʊə/ 诱惑；吸引力 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He couldn't resist the allure of the city lights.
vocabulary.translation: 他无法抗拒城市灯光的诱惑。

vocabulary.example: Good etiquette requires you to say "please" and "thank you".
vocabulary.translation: 良好的礼仪要求你说“请”和“谢谢”。

vocabulary.example: She took a selfie in front of the Eiffel Tower.
vocabulary.translation: 她在埃菲尔铁塔前自拍了一张。

vocabulary.entry: go cold turkey [phr.] /ɡəʊ kəʊld ˈtɜːki/ 突然戒掉 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He decided to go cold turkey and quit smoking immediately.
vocabulary.translation: 他决定突然戒烟，立即停止吸烟。

vocabulary.entry: switch off [phr.] /swɪtʃ ɒf/ 关掉；不再注意
vocabulary.example: Remember to switch off your phone during the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 记住在会议期间关掉手机。

vocabulary.entry: stare at [phr.] /steər æt/ 盯着；凝视
vocabulary.example: It's rude to stare at people.
vocabulary.translation: 盯着别人看是不礼貌的。

vocabulary.entry: in spite of [phr.] /ɪn spaɪt əv/ 尽管；不顾 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: In spite of the rain, they went for a walk.
vocabulary.translation: 尽管下雨，他们还是去散步了。

vocabulary.entry: keep alive [phr.] /kiːp əˈlaɪv/ 使继续存在 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: We must keep the tradition alive.
vocabulary.translation: 我们必须让这个传统继续下去。

sentences.english: How often do you check your phone?
sentences.chinese: 你多久查看一次手机呢？

sentences.english: According to a study led by Nottingham Trent University in Britain, the average person looks at their device 85 times a day, browsing the internet or using apps.
sentences.chinese: 根据英国诺丁汉特伦特大学主导的一项研究，普通人每天会查看自己的手机85次，浏览互联网或者使用应用程序。

sentences.english: Updating their status on social media platforms also made people reach for their electronic companion frequently.
sentences.chinese: 在社交媒体平台上更新自己的状态也使得人们频繁地拿起他们的电子伙伴（手机）。

sentences.english: Even the study's participants thought that was a lot: this figure is twice as often as they thought they did.
sentences.chinese: 甚至这项研究的参与者都认为这个次数很多：这个数字是他们认为的两倍。

sentences.english: Our phones might be shaping our behaviour more than we realise, and changing the way we interact with people right next to us.
sentences.chinese: 我们的手机对我们行为的塑造可能比我们意识到的要多，并且正在改变我们与身边人互动的方式。

sentences.english: Do you actually look at your surroundings more than at your phone?
sentences.chinese: 你实际上是更多地关注周围环境还是手机呢？

sentences.english: Is it rude to check your phone when someone is talking to you?
sentences.chinese: 当有人跟你说话时查看手机是不是不礼貌呢？

sentences.english: Sherry Turkle interviewed hundreds of college students about this.
sentences.chinese: 雪莉·特克尔就此采访了数百名大学生。

sentences.english: She's a clinical psychologist and a professor of social studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
sentences.chinese: 她是一名临床心理学家，也是麻省理工学院的社会学教授。

sentences.english: They talked about something they called 'the rule of three'.
sentences.chinese: 他们谈到了一个他们称之为“三规则”的东西。

sentences.english: The rule has to do with being considerate to others in spite of the allure of the little flat box.
sentences.chinese: 这个规则与在那个小小的扁平盒子（手机）的诱惑下仍然对他人体贴有关。

sentences.english: Turkle explains: "If you go to dinner with friends, you don't want to look down at your phone until you see that three people are looking up in the conversation.
sentences.chinese: 特克尔解释说：“如果你和朋友去吃晚餐，你不应该低头看手机，直到看到有三个人在抬头交谈。

sentences.english: So there's a new etiquette where you don't look down unless three people are looking up in order to keep a little conversation alive."
sentences.chinese: 所以有了一个新的礼仪，即你不要低头，除非有三个人抬头，这样才能让交谈继续下去。”

sentences.english: Actually, if you are clever enough you might use your phone as a tool to connect with people next to you.
sentences.chinese: 实际上，如果你足够聪明，你可以把手机当作与身边人建立联系的工具。

sentences.english: How about showing them pictures stored in its memory?
sentences.chinese: 给他们看看手机里存储的照片怎么样呢？

sentences.english: Sharing a bit of your life with them can bring you closer together.
sentences.chinese: 和他们分享一点你的生活可以让你们的关系更亲密。

sentences.english: And you can also invite everyone to take a selfie with you.
sentences.chinese: 你还可以邀请每个人和你一起拍自拍。

sentences.english: But the best thing to deal with mobile phone addiction is to go cold turkey and leave the machine behind occasionally or just switch it off and keep it firmly in your pocket for a while.
sentences.chinese: 但是应对手机成瘾的最好办法是突然戒掉，偶尔把手机放在一边，或者干脆关掉手机，把它牢牢地放在口袋里一段时间。

sentences.english: Who knows... 'life' might be what happens when you are too busy staring at a small screen.
sentences.chinese: 谁知道呢……当你忙于盯着小屏幕时，“生活”可能就在悄然流逝。
